evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking API change. The fix is internal to ModelManager::build_cache() routing-policy parsing. The new `allowed_origins` config field (visible in the diff) was part of the squash and is unrelated to this PR. No CLI contract, exported API, persistence format, or documented behavior changed.
evidence.documentation: No documentation changes required. The behavior is an internal fix; the only user-visible surface is a new warning log message for degraded routing, which does not warrant doc updates.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No dedicated manual to-do. The fix affects routing-cache resolution at startup for users who have router collections referencing classifiers on hardware-unavailable backends (e.g., ryzenai-llm on a non-NPU host). There is no CLI command, config option, or API endpoint that directly exercises this path; the behavior manifests only as a warning log from the affected router at startup. If the user has no router collection with such a classifier, the pre-filter snapshots are skipped entirely (the code checks for router collections first). The three regression tests with explicit hardware-filter premises cover the scenarios thoroughly.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The final approval was from @SlawomirNowaczyk at 2026-09-06T16:19:56Z. All PR branch commits predate this: the last PR branch commit is 4bc34558 dated 2026-09-03T06:23:19+0300. This commit introduced the shared `make_routing_parse_options()` resolver and the `unavailable_components` logging, which @SlawomirNowaczyk approved. No commits were added after approval. The PR was squash-merged into main on 2026-09-09T16:32:59Z.
evidence.review: Two reviewers with smart-router subject-matter expertise (per contribute.md: @fl0rianr and @SlawomirNowaczyk) conducted iterative reviews. @fl0rianr raised three edge cases across three rounds (Aug 28, Aug 28, Aug 29) — post-filter alias resolution, alias precedence mismatch, and missing builtin.<X> alias form — each addressed in a follow-up commit before final approval (Aug 30). @SlawomirNowaczyk suggested unifying the two routing-policy parse-site resolvers to prevent future drift (Aug 31, changes-requested); the author implemented this in commit 4bc34558 (Sep 3), and @SlawomirNowaczyk approved on Sep 6. No comments from the reviews were inline; all were on the PR body.
evidence.security: No security concern. The diff touches routing policy resolution and model alias computation — no credential handling, network calls, permission broadening, or supply-chain changes. The commit message and code are consistent with a genuine bug fix.
evidence.tests: Three new regression tests in test/cpp/test_model_manager_collection_validation.cpp: (1) canonical-id in components / bare-name on classifier, (2) bare-name in components / canonical-id on classifier, (3) builtin.<X> alias form using a real builtin. Each test asserts its hardware-filtered premise (!model_exists) before checking the policy, so tests won't go vacuously green on an NPU-capable CI. The tests also evaluate the parsed policy via RoutingPolicyEngine to confirm unrelated deterministic rules still route while the filtered classifier's rule falls back — not merely that parsing didn't abort.

shout_outs.reason: Identified three progressively deeper alias-resolution edge cases (bare-name alias, Registered/Imported/Builtin precedence, builtin.<X> prefix) across three comment rounds and iteratively guided the author to the correct shared-algorithm solution.

subject: fix(routing): don't drop the whole router policy over one hardware-filtered classifier (#3414)
summary: Fixes ModelManager::build_cache() so that a hardware-filtered classifier no longer drops the entire routing policy, instead allowing unrelated rules to survive via a pre-filter snapshot of model types and aliases.
verdict_reason: The fix addresses a real bug with thorough edge-case coverage (three regression tests with explicit hardware-filter premises), was iteratively reviewed by two smart-router experts, and no commits were added after the final approval.
